cover.hook: United Airlines will block AI agents from booking your flights.
cover.sub: United cites cybersecurity, privacy and possible legal violations. Sharing your login with an AI assistant is the problem.

slides.title: What United announced
slides.body: United will block AI agents from managing customers' reservations and buying flights, on its own platforms and through aggregators and agencies, with updates to its booking, ticketing and distribution policies (The Record, 12 Nov).

slides.title: The security reason
slides.body: United says sharing account credentials with third-party AI assistants 'can expose sensitive information', and their actions may cause unintended purchases, account changes or use of MileagePlus miles.

slides.label: is what United says not to give AI assistants
slides.note: Bank of America also cautioned users last week never to share user IDs and passwords with agents, per The Record.

slides.title: The legal reason
slides.body: United says automated AI actions could break FAA and DOT rules, because check-in requires human acknowledgment that bags don't contain banned items like explosives.

slides.title: Do this week
items: Never hand your password to an AI assistant
Check which agents have saved logins or tokens
Turn on MFA on travel and bank accounts
Review recent bookings and points activity

cover.hook: One accidental download. $28.8 million in ransomware losses.
cover.sub: The DOJ says Gootloader was the first infection for 44+ US ransomware victims. Now it's been taken down.

slides.title: What happened
slides.body: An international operation disrupted 235 servers and 257 domains used by Gootloader, CastleRAT and the StealC stealer. The DOJ says it removed Gootloader from more than 100 servers, including compromised websites, and seized domains (The Record, 13 Nov).

slides.title: How Gootloader worked
slides.body: Per unsealed court documents, victims usually downloaded it by accident from compromised websites, which added their device to a botnet. The operators then sold that access to ransomware gangs.

slides.label: losses across 44+ US ransomware victims
slides.note: DOJ figures as reported by The Record. Officials say Gootloader has infected 25,000 devices globally since 2018.

slides.title: Who it hit
slides.body: A Defense Department official said Gootloader targeted victims globally, including the Department of War and the Defense Industrial Base. Shadowserver worked with ISPs and CSIRTs to notify infected victims. It's part of Operation Endgame.

slides.title: Do this week
items: Treat loader alerts as pre-ransomware, not just malware
Block script files from running out of downloads
Check Shadowserver reports for your IP ranges
Hunt for odd JavaScript run by users after web searches

segments.show: Red Hat Quay CVE-2026-123710 (CVSS 9.8) lets an attacker add their own signing key and get tokens for any repository (The Hacker News, 12 Nov).

segments.say: No account needed. Anonymous access is on by default. They can read and overwrite images.
segments.show: Read private images and secrets inside them, push or overwrite images. The planted key survives restarts. Affects every Quay 3 and Quay 5 version, per Red Hat.

segments.say: Block the keys endpoint, remove unknown service keys, then patch.
segments.show: Red Hat: block /keys at the proxy, search audit logs for service_key_rotate events with no expiry, remove unknown keys, install the fix. Second flaw CVE-2026-110697 (CVSS 9.9).

#PatchNow #CyberSecurity
items.ig_caption:
CVSS 9.8. Every private image in your Quay registry. 🐳

What The Hacker News reported (12 Nov):
→ Red Hat Quay CVE-2026-123710 (CVSS 9.8) lets an attacker add their own signing key to Quay's trusted keys, with no expiry
→ Quay then accepts their tokens for any repository: they can read private images and the secrets inside, and push or overwrite images
→ Anonymous access is on by default, so no account is needed; the planted key survives restarts
→ A second flaw, CVE-2026-110697 (CVSS 9.9), lets a user who can create a namespace steal other tenants' robot tokens
→ Red Hat says every Quay 3 and Quay 5 version is affected; fixed builds are out for eight Quay 3 branches and Quay.io is fixed

Do this now: block the /keys endpoint at your proxy, search audit logs for service key rotations with no expiry, remove keys you don't recognise, then install the fixed release.
